profile.title: Nutrition Counseling for Obesity and Asthma Self-Management in a Precontemplative Patient with Hidden Medication Overuse and Recent Pregnancy Termination
profile.summary: This case places a dietetics student in a telehealth nutrition counseling visit with a proud, precontemplative patient referred for obesity and asthma management. Beyond the grazing eating pattern and wheat-allergy label-reading gaps, the core teaching points are eliciting a hidden medication-use mismatch (chart-documented PRN diphenhydramine versus her actual near-nightly use) through sensitive, non-judgmental questioning, and practicing motivational interviewing with a patient who resists any framing that something needs to change, while respecting a recent, undisclosed pregnancy termination that should surface only if she chooses to share it.
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit, patient at home in Paramus, New Jersey, on a short break between shifts

patient.name: Elsy Boyer
patient.occupation: Shift supervisor at a dry-cleaning and laundry service
patient.appearance: A stocky, central-weight-gain build; visibly tired by late afternoon but sits upright and speaks briskly, often smiling or joking. Calling from a cluttered kitchen table with laundry baskets visible in the background, phone propped against a cereal box, occasionally glancing offscreen toward kids' noise in another room.

persona.personality: Proud, self-reliant, quick with a joke to deflect anything that feels like criticism or pity; dislikes being told what to do, especially about her body or her habits; genuinely warm and resourceful under the brisk exterior
persona.communicationStyle: Keeps things light and brisk, plain practical language, no medical jargon; redirects to her job or her church group whenever a question gets too close to something uncomfortable; answers quickly and moves the conversation along
persona.emotionalState: Outwardly upbeat and energetic, cracking jokes, but visibly tired by late afternoon; becomes guarded and stiffens briefly if reproductive health or recent personal stress is touched on, then quickly redirects
persona.background: Elsy grew up working-class in northern New Jersey, did some community college business courses before moving into retail and service management, and now works full-time as a shift supervisor at a dry-cleaning and laundry service. She's a single mother raising eight kids and takes real pride in having kept her household fed and running on her own. She and several of her kids attend a nondenominational church most Sundays, where the potluck dinners and prayer groups are one of the only places she feels fully supported without being judged - she's famous there for her baked ziti.
speechExamples: Oh, I'm fine, I'm always fine - ask anybody at the laundromat.
Honestly between work and the kids I eat whenever I can grab something, you know how it is.
I've been doing just fine managing myself for 42 years, I think I've got it figured out.
That's old news, let's talk about something else - how about I tell you about the potluck we had Sunday?
It's just an allergy pill, it's not like it's anything serious.
concerns: Being judged for her weight or her eating habits
Having to explain her recent pregnancy termination to anyone outside her closest circle
Running out of her asthma medication at an inconvenient time at work

scenario.studentBrief: You are a dietetics student conducting a telehealth nutrition counseling visit with Elsy Boyer, a 42-year-old woman referred for nutrition counseling related to weight and asthma management. Review her available health record before the call, then conduct a nutrition assessment and begin patient-centered counseling.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Referred for nutrition counseling related to weight and asthma management
scenario.openingLine: Hi there! Sorry if there's noise in the background, kids are home. So I guess my doctor wants me talking to you about my weight and my asthma, but honestly I feel pretty fine most days - between the laundromat and the house I don't really have time to think about it much!
tasks: Take a focused nutrition history including a 24-hour recall and typical eating/meal pattern
Review relevant anthropometric, vital sign, and laboratory data from her health record and relate them to her nutrition status
Explore her medication-taking patterns and food allergy management in a non-judgmental way to identify any gaps between what's prescribed and what's actually happening
Apply motivational interviewing techniques to engage a patient who does not currently see her habits as a problem
Document an ADIME note summarizing your assessment, nutrition diagnosis, and an initial, patient-centered plan

actions.name: 24-hour dietary recall
actions.result: Patient reports no fixed breakfast/lunch/dinner. Grazes on pretzel rods and string cheese from breakroom vending machine during shifts, reheated spaghetti or sloppy joes left from feeding her kids, frozen waffles or toast eaten standing up before work, and iced coffee with flavored creamer throughout the day. Reports a larger meal around 9-10pm after younger children are in bed. Minimal plain water intake.

actions.name: Weight history and goals assessment
actions.result: Patient states her weight is 'just how her body is built' after having several children and does not identify her weight as a concern needing intervention. Reports no current attempts at weight change.

actions.name: Readiness-to-change / stage of change assessment
actions.result: Patient does not perceive her eating pattern, weight, or medication use as problems. Minimal interest expressed in setting behavior-change goals at this time; redirects to work schedule and church activities when change is suggested.

actions.name: Food allergy and label-reading practices review
actions.result: Patient reports a lifelong diagnosed wheat allergy causing diarrhea on exposure. States she 'knows her allergies' from a lifetime of experience and does not consistently read ingredient labels on packaged snack foods, relying instead on recognizing familiar brands. Describes occasional mild stomach upset after snack foods that she attributes to 'just a stomach thing.'

actions.name: Physical activity assessment
actions.result: Patient reports being on her feet most of her 8-hour shift lifting and sorting laundry but no structured exercise outside of work. States she feels 'too tired' after work for additional activity.

actions.name: Sleep pattern assessment
actions.result: Patient reports trouble staying asleep most nights due to itching from her skin condition and occasional nighttime coughing.

actions.name: Hydration assessment
actions.result: Patient reports drinking mostly iced coffee with flavored creamer and occasional soda through the day; says she 'forgets' plain water most days.

actions.name: Household food access and budget assessment
actions.result: Patient reports stretching groceries for a household of eight on a tight budget, relying on a loyalty card at a local discount grocery store, and says the income figure on her chart 'doesn't match what's left after bills.'

actions.name: Asthma and dermatitis medication adherence review
actions.result: Patient reports using her daily budesonide nebulizer inconsistently, 'when her chest feels tight' rather than every day, citing the time the nebulizer setup takes before her shift. Reports using her albuterol rescue inhaler fairly reliably but worries about running out at work. Reports taking diphenhydramine as needed, often at night, for itching, and describes it as 'just an allergy pill' when asked how often she uses it.

actions.name: Review pharmacy refill history
actions.result: Diphenhydramine 25 mg tablets: refill quantities and frequency consistent with near-daily use over the past several months, exceeding typical as-needed dosing patterns.

actions.name: Review allergy list in chart
actions.result: Mold, animal dander, grass pollen, tree pollen, wheat (diarrhea), shellfish (skin eruption).

actions.name: Review household demographics and insurance on file
actions.result: Household of 8 in Paramus, NJ. Insurance: Medicare. Reported household income figure on file does not reflect self-reported day-to-day grocery budget.

objectives.text: Elicit a 24-hour food recall and typical eating pattern from a patient with an irregular, grazing eating pattern, identifying lack of structured meals, reliance on convenience snacks, and a large late-evening meal
Relate anthropometric, vital sign, and laboratory data to nutrition status, including BMI classification, recent weight change, and lipid/CBC results
Explore medication-taking patterns non-judgmentally to identify gaps between prescribed regimen and actual use, including asthma controller underuse and antihistamine overuse
Assess food allergy management and label-reading practices in the context of a diagnosed wheat allergy and frequent packaged-snack consumption
Apply motivational interviewing techniques to engage a precontemplative patient who does not perceive her habits as a problem and dislikes being told what to do
Recognize the dual role of faith community and household financial/food-access constraints as both strengths and barriers in building a patient-centered nutrition plan

answerKey.primaryProblem: Excessive energy intake / irregular eating pattern (grazing, skipped structured meals, large late-evening meal) in the context of obesity (BMI 30.7), poorly controlled asthma, and chronic atopic dermatitis, in a precontemplative patient
differential: Food- and nutrition-related knowledge deficit regarding wheat allergy and label reading
Inconsistent asthma controller medication use contributing to nocturnal symptoms (nutrition-relevant via fatigue/energy balance, not itself a dietetics diagnosis)
Behavioral barrier: limited readiness to change (precontemplation) limiting intervention uptake
Food access/resource barrier despite documented household income not matching lived reality
keyFindings: BMI 30.7 kg/m2 (height 162.2 cm, weight 80.7 kg), up 1.9 kg since 2025-02-08
No fixed meal structure; grazes all day on vending-machine/convenience snacks with one large meal around 9-10pm
Minimal plain water intake; hydration mainly iced coffee with flavored creamer
Diagnosed wheat allergy (diarrhea) but inconsistent label-reading on packaged snack foods; occasional mild GI symptoms she attributes to 'just a stomach thing'

Chart documents diphenhydramine 25mg as PRN/occasional nighttime use per patient report; patient's own description in conversation reveals near-nightly use for months to control itching - this is the mismatch to surface, not resolve on this call
Mild expiratory wheeze and reports of occasional nighttime cough/chest tightness, with inconsistent daily budesonide use ('when her chest feels tight' rather than daily)
Lipids within normal limits (TC 152.8, LDL 98.7, TG 115.5) except low HDL 31 mg/dL (ref >=40)
Hemoglobin, WBC, platelets all within normal reference ranges
Precontemplative stance: 'this is just how my body is built,' resists framing suggesting a problem
Church potlucks (e.g., her baked ziti) are both a strong social support and a recurring source of calorie-dense, less structured eating
plan: Complete a structured ADIME nutrition assessment including a detailed 24-hour recall and typical day pattern, documenting grazing behavior, skipped sit-down meals, and the late large evening meal
Discuss hydration pattern and encourage gradual increase in plain water intake alongside her usual iced coffee, in a non-prescriptive way consistent with her readiness stage
Review her wheat allergy label-reading habits for packaged/vending snacks and provide practical, non-judgmental education on identifying wheat-containing ingredients

Use motivational interviewing to explore her own goals (staying able to work full-time, keeping her household fed) and gently raise ambivalence about current habits without directly challenging her belief that nothing needs to change

Note the discrepancy between the documented PRN diphenhydramine use and her description of near-nightly use; reflect this back supportively and recommend she discuss actual frequency with her prescribing provider rather than counseling on dosing herself
Identify her church community as a resource to build on (e.g., collaborating on potluck dish choices) rather than a barrier to eliminate
Explore practical, low-cost strategies for more consistent meal timing given her shift schedule and household size, respecting her stated budget constraints
Plan a follow-up visit to continue rapport-building before introducing more specific behavior-change goals, given her precontemplative stage
redFlags: Near-nightly, months-long use of an antihistamine for itch/sleep that has not been disclosed to her prescriber - needs medical follow-up, not nutrition management
Inconsistent use of daily controller asthma medication alongside reported nighttime cough and wheeze on exam - relevant to refer back to her prescriber/respiratory care team

Recent (within months) pregnancy termination with no current disclosure to work or most of her church community - acknowledge supportively if she raises it, do not probe, and avoid documenting unnecessary detail beyond what she chooses to share
educationPoints: Plain language explanation of how regular, structured meals/snacks may help with energy levels and could support more consistent asthma symptom control, framed around her own stated goal of getting through shifts without flare-ups
Practical tips for reading ingredient labels on packaged snacks to identify wheat, geared to her literacy level and shopping habits (e.g., discount grocery loyalty card items)
Validating her resourcefulness in feeding a household of eight while gently introducing the idea of occasional lower-cost, less processed swaps where feasible

Normalizing that medication questions (including how often an as-needed medicine is actually being used) are best worked through with her prescriber, and offering to help her prepare for that conversation
Affirming her church community as a strength while discussing collaborative strategies (e.g., contributing a lower-sodium or vegetable-forward dish) rather than framing potlucks as something to avoid

mismatches.patientClaim: Elsy describes her diphenhydramine use as 'just an allergy pill' she takes as needed, often at night, downplaying how often she actually uses it (h23/h24)
mismatches.recordEvidence: Pharmacy refill history shows refill quantities and frequency consistent with near-daily use over the past several months, exceeding typical as-needed dosing patterns (d4)
mismatches.teachingPoint: Patients may sincerely under-report frequency of an 'as needed' medication they've normalized into daily use; refill/pharmacy records can reveal a pattern the patient themselves may not recognize as significant, prompting a non-judgmental referral back to the prescriber rather than independent dose counseling.

mismatches.patientClaim: Elsy reports using her daily budesonide nebulizer only when her chest feels tight, not daily, citing time constraints before her shift (h21)
mismatches.recordEvidence: Current Medication List documents budesonide 0.25 mg/mL inhalation suspension prescribed as a daily maintenance nebulizer treatment for asthma (d1)
mismatches.teachingPoint: A gap between prescribed frequency documented in the medication list and patient-reported as-needed use signals controller medication underuse; dietetics clinicians should recognize this as relevant to fatigue/energy balance and flag it for the prescribing team rather than attempt to adjust dosing themselves.
